card.title: Universe: Big Bang and Hubble's Law

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The Big Bang theory describes the universe originating from an extremely hot, dense state ~13.8 billion years ago and expanding ever since. Hubble's Law v = H₀d states that galaxies recede at speeds proportional to their distance, providing direct evidence for cosmic expansion. The Hubble constant H₀ ≈ 70 km/s/Mpc quantifies the current expansion rate.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Hubble's Law: $v = H_0 d$
Redshift: $z = \frac{\lambda_{obs} - \lambda_{emit}}{\lambda_{emit}} = \frac{a(t_{now})}{a(t_{emit})} - 1$
Hubble time: $t_H = \frac{1}{H_0}$

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Homogeneity and Isotropy: Cosmological principle assumes universe looks same everywhere (homogeneous) and in all directions (isotropic) on large scales (>100 Mpc). Validated by CMB uniformity and galaxy surveys.  ·  General Relativity Framework: Expansion described by Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker metric derived from Einstein's field equations. Newtonian mechanics insufficient for cosmological scales.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Statement 1: Hubble's Law provides observational evidence that the universe is expanding uniformly.  ·  Statement 2: Cosmic microwave background radiation confirms the hot Big Bang origin of the universe.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Galaxy at d = 100 Mpc: v = 70 × 100 = 7000 km/s. Redshift z ≈ v/c = 7000/300000 ≈ 0.023.  ·  Hubble time: t_H = 1/(70 km/s/Mpc) = 1/(2.27×10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹) ≈ 4.4×10¹⁷ s ≈ 14.0 Gyr.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Thinking Big Bang was explosion IN space: It was expansion OF space itself — no pre-existing void.  ·  Believing galaxies move THROUGH space: Comoving galaxies are stationary; space stretches between them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Big Bang Theory: The universe began as a singularity of infinite density and temperature approximately 13.8 × 10⁹ years ago. Space itself expanded, cooling the universe and allowing formation of subatomic particles, atoms, stars, and galaxies over time.  ·  Cosmic Timeline: t = 0: Singularity. t < 10⁻⁴³ s: Planck epoch (quantum gravity). t ~ 10⁻³⁶ s: Inflationary epoch (exponential expansion). t ~ 3 min: Nucleosynthesis (H, He, Li formed). t ~ 380,000 yr: Recombination (CMB released). t ~ 400 Myr: First stars. t ~ 9 Gyr: Solar system forms.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: v = H₀d: linear relation between speed and distance.  ·  Higher z → farther away → older lookback time.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q1. State Hubble's Law and explain its significance for cosmology.  ·  Q2. Describe three lines of evidence supporting the Big Bang theory.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: State Hubble's Law with units: H₀ in km/s/Mpc, d in Mpc, v in km/s.  ·  Explain why redshift is cosmological, not Doppler, for distant galaxies.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Universe originated ~13.8 Gyr ago from hot, dense state (Big Bang).  ·  Hubble's Law v = H₀d proves cosmic expansion.  ·  CMB at 2.725 K is relic radiation from recombination epoch.  ·  Redshift measures expansion of space, not Doppler motion.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Edwin Hubble published his law in 1929; Georges Lemaître derived it theoretically in 1927 from general relativity.  ·  The observable universe has radius ~46.5 billion light-years despite age 13.8 Gyr due to expansion during light travel.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Q3. Distinguish cosmological redshift from Doppler redshift.  ·  Q4. Calculate recession velocity of a galaxy 250 Mpc away (H₀ = 70 km/s/Mpc).  ·  Q5. What is the cosmic microwave background and why is it important?

rows.text: List and explain three key evidences for Big Bang theory.  ·  Discuss implications of accelerated expansion for fate of universe.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: CMB peak wavelength: λ_max = 2.9 mm·K / 2.725 K ≈ 1.06 mm (microwave region).  ·  Lookback time for z = 1: Light emitted when universe was half its current size (~7.7 Gyr ago).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Evidence for Big Bang: (1) Hubble's Law — galaxies receding proportionally to distance. (2) Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) — 2.725 K blackbody radiation, uniform to 1 part in 10⁵. (3) Abundance of light elements — H:He ratio ~3:1 matches nucleosynthesis predictions. (4) Large-scale structure — galaxy distribution matches gravitational growth from initial fluctuations.  ·  Hubble's Law: v = H₀d, where v is recession velocity, d is proper distance, and H₀ is Hubble constant. Discovered by Edwin Hubble in 1929 using Cepheid variable stars as standard candles. Current best estimate: H₀ ≈ 67–74 km/s/Mpc (tension between CMB and local measurements).  ·  Interpretation of Redshift: Cosmological redshift z = Δλ/λ is NOT Doppler shift from motion through space. It results from stretching of photon wavelengths as space expands during transit. For small z: v ≈ cz; for large z: relativistic cosmology required.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Scale factor relation: $1 + z = \frac{a(t_0)}{a(t)}$  ·  Friedmann equation: $H^2 = \frac{8\pi G}{3}\rho - \frac{kc^2}{a^2} + \frac{\Lambda c^2}{3}$  ·  Critical density: $\rho_c = \frac{3H_0^2}{8\pi G}$

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Redshift-Distance Relation Linear Only Locally: v = H₀d holds for z < 0.1. Higher redshifts require full relativistic treatment with scale factor a(t) and cosmological parameters Ω_m, Ω_Λ.  ·  Hubble Constant Tension: Local distance ladder (Cepheids + SNe Ia) gives H₀ ≈ 73 km/s/Mpc; CMB (Planck satellite) gives H₀ ≈ 67.4 km/s/Mpc. Discrepancy unresolved — possible new physics or systematic errors.  ·  Dark energy drives accelerated expansion discovered in 1998.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: H₀ tension between local and CMB measurements remains unsolved.  ·  Assuming universe expands into something: There is no 'outside' — spacetime is self-contained.  ·  Confusing Hubble flow with peculiar motion: Local gravitational interactions cause deviations from pure Hubble flow.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Thinking CMB comes from stars: It predates star formation by hundreds of millions of years.  ·  1 Mpc = 3.26 million light-years = 3.086 × 10²² m.  ·  CMB was accidentally discovered by Penzias and Wilson in 1965 (Nobel Prize 1978).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Georges Lemaître first proposed expanding universe and 'primeval atom' hypothesis in 1927, before Hubble's observations.  ·  NEB asks to explain Hubble's Law, interpret redshift, and list evidence supporting Big Bang theory.  ·  Statement 3: Cosmological redshift arises from expansion of space, not relative motion through space.
